A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlashAttention training-failure analysis and mitigation. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms and appendices support a reliable comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 training experiments, precision-substitution interventions, representation and gradient analyses, and stabilization trials, including Figures 2–7.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical analyses and reports longer GPT-2 training experiments, Llama-3.1-8B representation probes, and the relationship between multiple maxima and loss.

M1.justification: Section 4 changes repeated-maximum detection from exact equality to a tolerance condition, rowmax(S) − S ≤ epsilon, with 10^-3 given as an example. This broadens when stabilization activates while retaining the same conditional softmax-shift mechanism.

E1.justification: OpenWebText language modeling remains the dataset/task coverage. The additions vary model size, architecture and optimizer, and inspect existing attention-pattern questions on illustrative English text; they do not establish a distinct data domain, language or task requirement.

E2.justification: Original FlashAttention remains the comparator against stabilized FlashAttention in Figure 7. The standard-attention and high-precision substitution comparisons in Section 3.2 are retained. Muon supplies an optimizer setting for both attention methods, rather than an additional competing stabilization method.

E3.justification: v1 Figure 7 shows training through 20K steps with beta = 7. v3 reports 600K-step GPT-2S experiments with beta = 2 under AdamW and Muon, plus 100K-step GPT-2M training under AdamW. These substantially extend the evaluation budgets and configurations; the original Section 3.1 setup remains documented.

E4.justification: v3 adds optimizer/model-size robustness checks in Figure 7, Llama-3.1-8B case studies of similar update structures and multiple maxima in Appendix D, and a temporal analysis of maxima occurrences versus loss in Appendix E.1/Figure 13. The original operation-, layer- and head-localization analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 7 explicitly displays Trial 1 and Trial 2 for each attention method. v3 replaces these with one displayed curve per method in each configuration without identifying repeated-run counts or uncertainty aggregation. Explicit replication information is therefore removed; this does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Figure 7 replaces the original two-trial results with longer trajectories across three configurations, reporting stable modified-attention training and loss explosions with original attention. New appendix results show corresponding attention patterns in Llama and a temporal relationship between maxima and loss. These are new or replaced results under different settings, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.3.2 substantially revises the central rounding argument. v1 incorrectly rounds the exact tie −4.703125 to −4.71875; v3 introduces an accumulated FP32 residual, giving −4.703990459442139 and a valid rounding-up example involving the sticky bit. Claim 3 and Remark 1 are correspondingly revised. Appendix E.2 expands the already-existing Equation 1 without changing its mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding summary retain the same central contributions: a mechanistic explanation involving similar low-rank updates and biased rounding, a minimal FlashAttention mitigation, and a diagnostic workflow. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 proposes that QK normalization and Gated Attention disrupt structurally aligned error updates, interprets rising maxima counts as a leading indicator of failure, and explicitly cautions that the Llama patterns do not demonstrate BF16 training failure. The existing GPT-2-focused and precision-format limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies Muon hyperparameters and parameter assignments, Llama probe details, and an explanation of absorbed attention scaling. Its pseudocode repairs the overwritten stabilization maximum and the backward dK update. These improve the documented implementation; the PDFs do not establish corresponding changes to previously executed code. The code link and original hardware details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Muon references by Jordan et al. (2024) and Liu et al. (2025), removes Hao et al. (2025), and adds an explanatory FlashAttention subsection in Appendix A.3. The broader related-work positioning and central novelty claim remain stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v3 locally rewrites the rounding and mitigation explanations, clarifies gradient notation, and expands supporting explanations through Appendix A.3, the detailed Equation 1 derivation and diagnostic workflow. It also adds future-work, acknowledgment and LLM-use text.

P2.justification: Figure 7 changes from one plot with labeled trials to three configuration panels with logarithmic training-step axes and revised legends. v3 adds two multipanel Llama figures and a dual-axis maxima/loss figure. Existing Figures 8–10 become Figures 10–12, and algorithms and several figures are repositioned; these retained displays are not new results.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves important correctness and reproducibility deficiencies: Section 3.3.2 repairs the invalid ties-to-even example, and the stabilized algorithm now preserves its adjusted maximum. Longer training across optimizer and model-size configurations substantially strengthens empirical support. The loss of explicit two-trial reporting reduces transparency, and the Llama evidence remains illustrative, but these limitations do not outweigh the central corrections and stronger validation.
